description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotional categories in a dataset used for evaluating speaker anonymization on emotional speech, with six distinct emotion labels represented by colored segments. The largest segment, labeled “Frustration,” occupies 25.1% of the chart and is colored light blue. The second largest, “Neutral,” accounts for 23.1% and is shown in dark blue. “Happiness” makes up 14.1% and is colored red, while “Sadness” comprises 14.7% and is orange. “Anger” represents 14.9% and is yellow. A small segment labeled “8.1%” appears in light blue next to “Happiness,” but its corresponding emotion label is not visible in the chart — it may correspond to an unlabeled or partially obscured category. The chart includes percentage values inside each slice and uses a simple color-coded legend implied by the labels adjacent to each segment. No slice is exploded or emphasized visually beyond its proportional size. The segments are arranged clockwise starting from the top with “Frustration,” and appear roughly ordered by decreasing magnitude, though “Sadness” and “Anger” are very close in size.
